notes: Strongest trap architecture in the batch and the most complete teaching payload: all twenty options carry a real, named misconception and every rationale supplies a quotable killing sentence. q1 outside-knowledge-in-passage-furniture (a drying charge exists, no price history does) / detail-as-main (Grendisham's unmanned-site objection promoted to topic, borrowing the coda's 'no one there to watch') / title-plausible theme never argued; q2 the conventional expectation the swabs defeated, a quantifier upgrade onto an invented age axis, and an over-hedged unsupported limitation; q3 position reversal recycling the controller vocabulary, a fabricated scope limit ('only'), and true-of-many-logs outside knowledge; q4 a softened miscount, a policy leap that also puts the lever in the wrong hands, an unstated capacity claim; q5 measured overclaim, neutral-reporter misread, verdict-turned-recommendation. Family mix is the blueprint's long_passage_5q exactly (TYPE-004 at edge position 1, 2x TYPE-001, TYPE-002, TYPE-005), keys D/B/C/A/C, key strict-longest 0 of 5. Arithmetic fact-checked: 61-49=12 = one fire in five, and 44 of 61 against a third of capacity, both as the rationales state. FIX 1 (calibration honesty, major): this unit states NO adversarial blind floor anywhere - not in gen-elf-long.NOTES.md, not in generator_meta - while carrying five G-STEM r3 flags. The policy (BRIEF-ADDENDUM, batch16 dom 1) requires the floor stated explicitly and no better than 1-in-2. It is the only unit in the batch with no floor at all. Worse, G-STEM r3's blind picks land ON THE KEY in four of the five (q1 D, q3 C, q4 A, q5 C; only q2's blind pick A misses), and q3 is classed WORLD_KNOWLEDGE - ordinary knowledge that a fire-brigade log timestamps the call-out rather than ignition decides q3 with no passage, which is BETTER than 1-in-2 and therefore outside the tolerated band. Declare floors per question, name q3's world-knowledge route explicitly, and route q3 to adjudication rather than shipping it silent. No option, key or stem touched; no re-gate. FIX 2 (law-10 accounting, minor): the hedge_balance field uses the HOUSE metric ('pick-the-qualified-option selects the key in 1 of 5') - correct instrument - but attributes it to the wrong question. It credits q4, whose key ('the same commercial pressure then, whatever they own') carries a UNIVERSALISING frame that points the absolutizer heuristic AWAY from the key (G-STEM r3 says exactly this), and discounts q5 on the ground that distractor D shares a 'scoped qualifier' - but 'convinced enough to' is an intensifier, not a hedge, and C is the only two-sided option against three committed stances, which is precisely G-STEM r3's blind pick and its named heuristic. Honest count: the key is selected on q5, arguably also on q1 (D is the only both-halves main-idea shape), so 1-2 of 5 - still at or under the half ceiling, so law 10 substantively HOLDS. Only the attribution is wrong; swapping q4 for q5 in the field is the whole fix. FIX 3 (rationale precision, minor): q4's key universalises one step past the passage's own mechanism. The text explains that custom operations work the tail 'because that is when the work is there, which is why their machines fill the log' - an asymmetry between custom and own-crop operations - while the key asserts the pressure is the same 'whatever they own'. What is genuinely common is the deduction schedule and the closing delivery window; the volume is not. Tighten the rationale clause 'the squeeze in those days is common to everyone drying' to name the schedule and the window as the shared term. No option text changes. Carried G-STEM r3 residuals reviewed and accepted as design: q4's crossing tells (the absolutizer heuristic points away from key A while the 'implied' shape heuristic points toward it - the two cross rather than align, which is what keeps the question alive) and q5's B-vs-C narrowing (strict authorial neutrality is an equally canonical attitude key, so form narrows to two and does not decide) are both honest 1-in-2 surfaces once declared. Neither is repairable without a redesign and neither needs one.

Fact-checked all twenty collocation/polarity claims in the five rationales against real English - the Batch-1 failure mode this stage exists to catch - and every one is true. Gap 1: 'take the long view' is the only assembly; 'take the long outlook' has no reading despite 'a long-term outlook' being real, 'long sight'/'long-sighted' exist but not in this frame and carry the ophthalmic sense, and a gaze is held/met/returned but not taken - all correctly stated. Gap 3: 'waiting for dead men's shoes' is the fixed proverb, and the hat/coat/glove analysis is right (each sits in real idioms - at the drop of a hat, kid gloves, the gloves are off - none of which is about succession, waiting or the dead). The fleet-repair-1 boots-to-hats swap is exactly the discipline law 4 asks for: 'fill someone's boots' and 'die with one's boots on' are both live idioms of succession AND of death, so 'boots' was a second defensible key rather than a lure, and the generator says so in the rationale. Gap 5: 'invoke a rule' is the verb English uses; evoke takes a memory/image/feeling, summon takes a person or a meeting, provoke takes a reaction - all three true, and the one-letter evoke/invoke pair is the correct choice of strongest lure. Gap 4 is a genuine polarity item: 'not approving, but not ___ either' puts both terms on one scale and demands the opposite pole, so 'gracious' as polarity_mirror (same side, leaving the 'but' nothing to carry) is right, and cautious/anxious are correctly diagnosed as wrong-AXIS rather than wrong-pole. Law 10: hedge_map uses the HOUSE metric and self-reports honestly against its own interest - 'the qualified/moderate heuristic selects the key in 1 of 5 questions', naming gap 2 ('Strictly') as the one place it lands. Gaps 1/3/5 are lexical-idiom gaps where hedging is not in play at all, and gap 4 is engineered against the heuristic (the key is the severe unsoftened word; both mild options are wrong). 1 of 5 is comfortably under the ceiling. G-STEM passed all five gaps in both rounds - the only unit in the batch to do so - and the r1 G-DISTRACTOR flag on gap 3 is the boots defect, repaired. Family mix per blueprint: 3 collocation / 1 polarity / 1 connective, meeting section 2's at-least-one-of-each; the blueprint reads 'connective/adverb gap', so 'Strictly' as a sentence-initial disjunct qualifies, and each of its three rivals dies on a QUOTABLE textual line rather than on feel (Increasingly on 'the clause as written' and the absence of any dating; Curiously on 'nobody disputes it or finds it odd'; Privately on 'Nothing here is hidden'), which is what lifts it above a vocabulary gap. Construct note, no defect: gaps 1, 3 and 5 are answerable from idiom knowledge without reading the passage, which is inherent to the settled ELF-CLOZE-001 construct (lexical/collocational competence), and gaps 2 and 4 do require the text. Nothing to fix.

Item design is strong for a one-question short. The mechanism was verified before drafting and holds: a pot raised a course above its neighbours belongs to a flue that smoked (usually the shortest flue, from the attic bedroom, with least warm air beneath it), and a narrowed mouth is a DRAUGHT ACCELERATOR, not a rain-and-vermin guard - so distractor B is built on the commonest lay belief about anything fitted to a chimney top and dies on the passage's own 'the same gases leave faster through less of an opening'. C is a clean true-idea-from-the-wrong-place trap (it keeps the real proposition - something on the stack indexes the problem flue - and attaches it to the feature the passage explicitly disqualifies with the flat 'Pattern tells you very little' plus three non-diagnostic causes), and D is plausible outside knowledge that the passage runs against (ornament was bought to tell one door from thirty identical ones). Rule 10 is broken cleanly on the single question: key A is flat, unhedged and specific, the ONLY hedged option is B ('mainly') and it is wrong, so pick-the-qualified scores 0 of 1. Lengths 14/15/14/15 - key tied for shortest, ratio 1.07. FIX (calibration honesty, major): the declared floor is 'no better than 1-in-4 - no option is strikeable on form, no option is the lone hedged or lone flat one, the key is tied-shortest, and lay priors actively select D or B'. The carried G-STEM r2 flag refutes the 'no option is strikeable on form' clause and supplies TWO routes to the key that the floor does not accommodate. (a) WORLD_KNOWLEDGE: raising one pot on a stack to cure a shy flue is standard vernacular building practice, and a domain reader also strips B because the narrowed mouth is a draught device - blind pick A, the key. (b) FORM-ONLY, needing no domain knowledge: C restates A's schema (a visible feature on the stack indexes the problem flue) with an exotic cue and a SUPERLATIVE ('the most trouble'), and two options on one schema let a test-wise reader prefer the mundane member - again A. Route (b) matters most, because the NOTES' own draft note records rewriting C precisely so that 'no option is strikeable without the passage', holding the floor at 1-in-4 - and the replacement traded an explicit absolutizer ('Any') for a superlative that a test-wise solver strips just as readily. Restate the floor at 1-in-2, the tolerated maximum and therefore still inside policy, and name the A/C shared-schema convergence as its basis. Notes/metadata only - no option, key, stem or rationale touched, no re-gate.

A well-built one-inch inference: the passage sets two hour-counts and two letter-counts side by side and never joins them (13 hours and 412 against 6 hours and 390, both shops on one market place, both shutting when the evening cart went at eight), and the reader must supply the connection. Distractors are all instructive: A is the incentive misread the per-hour allowance invites, B is the law-11 corollary done right (the direction is true and the figures are the passage's own, but 'far more' is exactly what 22 letters refuse - a detail DISTORTED, never quoted faithfully), C is the compensation misread killed by one flat sentence. Rule 10 clean: key D is a flat unhedged causal assertion and the single qualified-sounding option ('much of his later start') is a distractor, so pick-the-moderate scores zero. Three options tie for longest, so there is no strict-longest option at all. FIX 1 (calibration honesty, major): the adversarial blind floor was never re-run after fleet-repair-1 rewrote option C, and its stated basis is now FALSE of the shipped sheet. The floor claims 'no better than 1 in 2 on any surface heuristic I could construct (three of the four options are contrastive X-rather-than-Y claims; the odd one out, B, is a comparative, and it is a distractor)'. That describes the retired C ('The hour of the evening cart was largely fixed to suit the shops'); on the shipped sheet only D has the contrastive shape, so 'pick the odd shape' now points AT the key rather than at a distractor. Appendix A re-ran rules 11 and 12, the hedge map, the option lengths and mech - but not the floor. Post-repair G-STEM r2 found the repair 'sharpened rather than softened the blind lean': B and C both presuppose that length of opening drives volume and D is the only option that names and rejects that premise, so the 'implied' stem plus the lone governing generalisation gives a reproducible no-expertise lean to the key. Restate the floor at 1-in-2 on the shared-presupposition basis and retire the stale option-shape sentence. Notes/metadata only. FIX 2 (rationale accuracy, minor): the rationale lists four documented facts and then asserts 'the six hours the two shops shared carried nearly four hundred at each counter'. That is documented for the BOOKSELLER only (all 390 fell in his six hours); the chandler's within-day distribution is unknown, and assuming it is the conclusion used as a premise. The teaching payload should read: seven extra hours of opening bought about twenty-two extra letters, so almost as many letters reached the bookseller's counter in six hours as reached the chandler's in thirteen. Same point, sound derivation. FIX 3 (rationale precision, minor): A's primary kill - 'An allowance that leaves one keeper at six hours and another at thirteen is not what settled either man's hours' - over-generalises into a non sequitur, since one incentive can produce two responses under two constraints. The valid kill is the one G-DISTRACTOR named across two rounds while holding A at ARGUABLE: A is a PLURAL, purposive claim about both keepers, and the bookseller's six hours on the identical allowance falsifies it, with no motive stated anywhere in the text. Lead with that. G-STEM's related minor - A is logically compatible with D (hours could be stretched for the allowance while the cart's hour still governed volume) - is correctly resolved: A is unsupported rather than false, which is the standard kill under an 'implied' stem, and no fix should touch A (any rewrite risks promoting it to DEFENSIBLE).

Best trap taxonomy in the batch: all sixteen options carry a correctly named operation and the labels actually fit - q1 scope_shift/reversed order (dig moved to late winter, roasting moved before storage), overgeneralisation ('Varje mosse' against the passage's explicit 'Langt ifran varje mosse'), over-hedged unsupported reservation; q2 a genuine reversed_causality (the same two quantities, opposite arrow), overgeneralisation ('Samtliga'), scope_shift method-as-result; q3 detail_as_main plus a dating over-extension, reversed_direction (water power was the hytta's condition, not the blastbruk's), scope_shift on the uppteckningar; q4 plausible_worldknowledge (the very interpretation the trials contradict), a measurement/interpretation confusion, and a textbook half_right_conjunction. Metallurgy fact-checked and correct throughout: ~1200 C melts fayalitic slag but not iron (>1500), CO from the charcoal draws oxygen from the ore grains, harder blast raises carbon pickup and carbon embrittles the bloom under the sledge, and an iron-POOR slag turns viscous at the temperatures such a furnace can hold so the iron in the waste is the price of the slag leaving the shaft at all. Family mix is the blueprint's LAS-long spec exactly (detaljhamtning text-ankrad, innehalls-ankrad, huvudbudskap/syfte, inferens). Key strict-longest 0 of 4. FIX 1 (law-10 metric, major): hedge_balance is stated in NON-STANDARD narrative form - 'keys on q1-q3 are confident, absolute-free specific claims; only q4's key is hedged (snarast)' - rather than the house metric, and it under-counts. Rule 13 names 'qualified / TWO-FACTOR / hedged' as one family, and q3's key D is the only 'bade X och Y' option in its set; G-STEM r3 independently flagged it as 'the only both-X-and-Y option, the usual shape of a which-statement-agrees-best key'. Restated in the house metric: pick-the-qualified/two-factor selects the key in 2 of 4 questions (q3's two-factor shape, q4's 'snarast'), which is EXACTLY the half ceiling - inside policy, but at it, not comfortably under it as the field implies. Batch18's review found that units reporting on a non-standard metric were the defective ones; this is that pattern, and the correction is arithmetic, not redesign. Note in the unit's favour: fleet-repair-3's rewritten q4-C ('Den ar omtvistad...') is itself measured and false, so q4's key is no longer the sole cautious-sounding option, and q1-D is a deliberately over-hedged FALSE distractor - both real rule-10 breaks. FIX 2 (calibration honesty, major): the section-6 adversarial blind floor was never re-run after fleet-repair-3 rewrote q3-B, q4-C and q4-D. Its q4 evidence describes the RETIRED C ('C is refuted twice (dating method; between-site variation)') - the shipped C is the measurement-versus-interpretation option and dies on a different sentence entirely. And its conclusions are contradicted by the r3 run that followed it: section 6 says 'Q3 A is at least as attractive as D to a non-reader' and 'Q4 A is the MORE attractive option to a non-reader, so the blind floor is below chance-plus', while G-STEM r3 reports blind pick = THE KEY on q2 (A), q3 (D) and q4 (B). Re-run and restate per question. Only q1 survives its original floor honestly, and it survives well: r3's blind pick there is A, a distractor, so the world-knowledge route MISSES the key. NOTE (comprehension vs recall, carried, not repairable here): q2 is the batch's most exploitable blind surface and r3 says so - A and B are exact physical inverses and school chemistry settles them (harder blast -> more carbon -> brittler iron), so a gymnasium student answers without reading. The passage does state the mechanism, and the distractors stay substantive, so this is world-knowledge answerability rather than a structural leak - but the honest disposition is to declare it at 1-in-1 for a domain solver and route it to adjudication, not to leave the stale '1-in-2 at best' claim standing. q3 and q4 carry the same class of route (history of technology; archaeometallurgy) at lower exploitability. Fixes 1 and 2 are metadata only - no option, key, stem or rationale text changes, no re-gate.

The item design is sound and the rule-10 work on q2 is exemplary: the key is flat, numeric and unhedged ('Sju av tio natter blev obetalda'), the cautious-sounding option B ('betalningsviljan svar att mata') is FALSE in substance because the passage reports a definite figure, and the only absolutizer sits on distractor C - so on q2 'qualified' and 'correct' point in opposite directions. On q1 the concessive two-part shape is shared by key D and distractor A, so it isolates nothing. Complement arithmetic checks out (31 % paid => ~7 in 10 unpaid). Family mix correct for a LAS short (one forfattarens_hallning, one enligt_texten_detalj). FIX 1 (calibration honesty, major): the rule-13 table AND the blind-floor derivation are both STALE - they describe an option that is no longer in the unit. Section 5 records q1-C as 'Utrustningen behovs, men...' and calls it 'a deliberate formal twin of the key'; section 7 builds the floor on it - 'C and D are formally indistinguishable, both concede the need and reject the fee... Adversarial blind field = {C, D} -> Honest adversarial blind floor: 1-in-2.' The SHIPPED q1-C is 'Forslaget bor genomforas som det ligger, eftersom badgasterna har nytta av utrustningen' - a flat single-clause ENDORSEMENT. The twin protection the floor rests on no longer exists. The number happens to survive, because A independently shares D's concessive shape, and G-STEM r2 re-derived exactly that post-repair ('D is the concessive need-yes-mechanism-no landing that stance questions conventionally key to; A shares the concessive shape, so this is a lean, not a decision'). But a floor whose stated basis has been retired is not a stated floor. Re-run section 5 and section 7 against the shipped sheet and rebase the 1-in-2 on {A, D}. FIX 2 (floor accuracy, minor): q2's declared floor of 1-in-3 is optimistic against the same gate run, which found that form alone strips B (a non-answer to a 'vad sags i texten' stem) and D (about a sign, not payment), leaving the A/C contradictory pair = 1-in-2. The item is nonetheless safe, because the cross-question corroboration then resolves that pair toward C, a DISTRACTOR - the blind route misses the key. Correct the number and record why the miss is the item's protection. FIX 3 (trap taxonomy, minor - these rationales become Layer-2 source material): two distractors carry the wrong operation label. q2-C ('Nastan alla natter blev betalda') is labelled 'reversed_causality / overdrift' but contains no causal arrow at all - it is a pole/complement inversion of a proportion (31 % read as 'nastan alla'), i.e. a quantifier inversion; the label's second half is right and the first half should go. q1-B is likewise labelled 'reversed_causality mot medgivandet' for what is actually a maintenance-instead-of-procurement misread - the text does describe two upkeep failures but demands two new bojar, a new stege and a hjartstartare, so it is a half_right/scope operation, not an inverted arrow. Mislabelling teaches the taxonomy wrong downstream. FIX 4 (rationale accuracy, minor): 'ratt storhet, vand riktning. 31 procent blir har nastan alla i stallet for EN DRYG FJARDEDEL'. 31 % is six points above a quarter and only two below a third; the natural and accurate Swedish anchor is 'knappt en tredjedel'. A student taking 'dryg fjardedel' as the reference gets the wrong mental figure for the very number the item turns on. PROVENANCE NOTE: q1-C, the passage and q1's rationale were all changed after generation, but generator_meta carries NO repair_log - unlike elf-b19-001/002 and las-b19-001, which all log their rounds. That absence is what let fixes 1 and 2 go unnoticed.

The shipped artifact is clean and this is the best law-10 work in the LAS lane, executed in both directions within one two-question unit. On q1 the hedged shape is DELIBERATELY shared: key D carries 'i regel' plus the scope clause 'dar skriften gick att jamfora', and distractor A carries 'i de flesta fall' plus 'tycks' - so the pick-the-hedged heuristic narrows to {A, D} and stops. On q2 the direction reverses: the key is a flat unhedged assertion while BOTH soft options are wrong - C ('omojlig att avgora') is the cautious-sounding one and D ('bada forklaringarna behovs') is the reflexive essay synthesis, which the text forecloses because none of the three mechanisms existed and there is nothing left to reconcile. Section 6 reports this in the HOUSE metric ('key hedged in 1 of 2 questions = exactly half, at the rule-10 ceiling and not over it') and states 1-in-2 per question with the correct bases - {A, D} on q1, the flat pair on q2 - which is exactly what G-STEM r2 derived independently ('A and D remain an explicit contradictory pair on who wrote the occupational word, which points the key into that pair by form'). G-STEM r2 PASSED q2 outright, the only non-cloze question in the batch to pass a second round, recording only that the four-way stance set (hold / abandon / undecidable / synthesise) has no lone hedge and that the residual pressure is the generic moderate-option heuristic which applies to authentic stance items too. Distractors are genuinely instructive: q1-B promotes the essay's one honest residue (the strike-throughs, which the text says could equally be changed decisions as corrected misreadings) into a settled finding, which is precisely what the author declines to do; q2-A quotes back 'holl fast vid misstanken lange' and the archivist dismissal, both true of the period BEFORE the test and reversed by 'Dar hade jag fel'. Family mix correct (one detalj_ospecificerad, one forfattarens_hallning). NOTE 1 (record sync, no conclusion moves): three places in gen-las-essa.NOTES.md still describe the RETIRED q1-B ('varje bevarad blankett') - the trap-plan table calls B 'overgeneralisation (scope deleted)', section 6 credits the unit's one hard absolutizer to it, and section 7's self-blind-solve kills it on a claim it no longer makes. The shipped rationale is correct for the option that actually ships (detail_as_main, killed by 'materialet svarar inte pa det'), and the rewrite only REMOVED a free blind elimination, so the floor and the hedge map both survive unchanged - which is why this is a note and not a fix. Sync the record anyway. NOTE 2 (label precision): 'plausible_worldknowledge' is the wrong head label twice. q1-C names the approved-title list, which is one of the ESSAYIST'S OWN three hypotheses stated in the passage and refuted in it ('ingen lista over godkanda ord') - an in-text hypothesis mistaken for a finding, not world knowledge. q2-D is a genre gesture, which the rationale itself calls 'den vanliga essagesten'. In both cases the prose gives the right mechanism and only the label is off; the prose is what students see, so this is cosmetic - but the labels feed family-level kill statistics. Same class of slip as 'reversed_causality (aktorsbyte)' on q1-A, where the parenthetical already supplies the correct operation (attribution/actor swap). NOTE 3 (provenance): as with las-b19-002, q1-B, the passage and both rationales changed after generation with no repair_log in generator_meta.
